facts_and_myths.explanation: Sleipnir was a living flesh-and-blood horse born naturally from Loki after his shapeshifting liaison.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Archaeological 8th-century Gotland picture stones frequently depict Odin riding an eight-legged horse.

name: Surtr
visual_anchor: Gigantic primordial fire giant wreathed in volcanic flames, raising an incandescent sword brighter than the sun above shattering rainbow gates.
core_traits: Primordial fire giant ruler of the southern burning realm Muspelheim
Guards Muspelheim with a flaming sword that burns brighter than the sun
Leads the sons of Muspell to shatter the Bifrost bridge at Ragnarok
Slays the unarmed god Freyr and consumes the entire cosmos in cleansing fire

facts_and_myths.claim: The volcanic island Surtsey off the southern coast of Iceland is named after Surtr.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When a new volcanic island formed from an ocean eruption in 1963, Icelanders named it Surtsey (Surtr's Island).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Surtr's name literally means 'the black' or 'the swarthy one', referencing charred soot.

facts_and_myths.claim: Surtr was created by Odin during the construction of Asgard.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Surtr existed before Odin and before the world was made, guarding the primordial fires of Muspelheim from the dawn of time.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His fiery destruction of the world allows a fresh, green Earth to rise renewed.

name: Ymir
visual_anchor: Colossal frozen primeval giant sleeping amidst swirling rime ice and boiling sparks where Niflheim and Muspelheim meet in the void.
core_traits: Primeval hermaphroditic giant and ancestor of all Jotnar (giants) in Norse myth
Formed in the cosmic void Ginnungagap where the ice of Niflheim met the heat of Muspelheim
Nourished by four rivers of milk flowing from the primordial cow Audhumbla
Slain by Odin, Vili, and Ve, who constructed the physical universe from his body

facts_and_myths.claim: According to Norse lore, the sky is made of Ymir's skull and the earth of his flesh.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Odin and his brothers fashioned earth from Ymir's flesh, mountains from bones, oceans from blood, and the sky dome from his skull.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Clouds were created by hurling Ymir's brains high into the atmosphere.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ymir was an Olympian titan who fought against Hercules.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ymir belongs strictly to Norse creation mythology, having no connection to Greek lore.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: When Ymir was slain, the flood of his blood drowned nearly all existing frost giants.

name: Nidhogg
visual_anchor: Sinister obsidian dragon coiled beneath mossy subterranean depths, gnawing maliciously upon the glowing root of Yggdrasil.
core_traits: Monstrous dragon or serpent dwelling in Niflheim beneath the World Tree Yggdrasil
Constantly gnaws at the deepest root of Yggdrasil, seeking to topple cosmic order
Trades taunts and insults with the eagle atop Yggdrasil via the messenger squirrel Ratatoskr
Feeds upon the corpses of perjurers, murderers, and adulterers in Nastrond

facts_and_myths.claim: At the conclusion of the Voluspa poem, Nidhogg is described flying over the post-Ragnarok world bearing corpses on his wings.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The closing stanza of Voluspa depicts Nidhogg rising from the dark rocks carrying the bodies of the dead upon his feathers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His name translates roughly to 'Malice Striker' or 'Tearer of Corpses'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Nidhogg was a guardian dragon who protected the roots of Yggdrasil from pests.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Nidhogg is a parasite and enemy of the World Tree, slowly rotting and eating away at its vital roots.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Multiple other serpents assist Nidhogg in gnawing Yggdrasil's roots.

name: Ratatoskr
visual_anchor: Chittering red squirrel with bushy tail scampering up the immense mossy bark of the cosmic ash tree Yggdrasil carrying gossip and taunts.
core_traits: Mythological squirrel scampering up and down the cosmic tree Yggdrasil
Acts as a messenger carrying insults between the unnamed eagle at the top and the dragon Nidhogg below
Stirs discord and fuels mutual hostility between the celestial eagle and subterranean dragon
Unique character in Norse mythology representing gossip and rumor-mongering

facts_and_myths.claim: Ratatoskr's name translates in Old Norse to 'Drill-Tooth' or 'Bore-Tooth'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Linguists trace 'rata' to bore or drill, referencing the gnawing habits of rodents through wood.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ratatoskr takes immense mischievous pleasure in keeping the dragon and eagle enraged at each other.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ratatoskr was a fire-breathing monster who devoured Viking warriors.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ratatoskr is an ordinary-looking red tree squirrel whose only weapon is sharp-tongued slander.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: He is depicted in modern video games like God of War Ragnarok and Smite.

name: Fafnir
visual_anchor: Armored venom-spitting dragon coiled atop a glittering hoard of golden arm-rings and gems, hissing down into a concealed earthen trench.
core_traits: Son of dwarf king Hreidmar transformed by greed into a monstrous dragon
Murdered his own father to claim the cursed gold of Andvari and the ring Andvaranaut
Wore the terrifying Aegis-helm (Helm of Awe) that struck horror into any who beheld it
Slain by hero Sigurd, who dug a pit beneath the dragon's path and thrust his sword Gram into its heart

facts_and_myths.claim: Sigurd gained the ability to understand the speech of birds after tasting Fafnir's roasted heart.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When testing if the dragon's heart was cooked, Sigurd burned his thumb, sucked the blood, and instantly understood the birds overhead.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The birds warned him that his mentor Regin planned to betray and assassinate him.

facts_and_myths.claim: Fafnir was born as a winged dragon who flew over the mountains of Norway.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fafnir was born a dwarf or giant with a human-like form, transformed into a wingless creeping lindworm by greed.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Fafnir and the cursed ring directly inspired J.R.R. Tolkien's Smaug and the One Ring.

name: Sigurd
visual_anchor: Golden-haired Germanic hero in fur mantle driving a reforged broadsword upward through the underbelly of a thrashing dragon.
core_traits: Greatest Germanic and Norse legendary hero of the Volsunga Saga and Nibelungenlied
Wielded the legendary sword Gram, reforged from the shattered pieces of his father's blade
Slew the greedy dragon Fafnir and claimed the cursed golden hoard of the Nibelungs
Bathed in dragon's blood to become invulnerable, except for a leaf-covered spot on his back

facts_and_myths.claim: In the Nibelungenlied, a linden leaf fell onto Sigurd's back while bathing in dragon blood, leaving a vulnerable spot.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Much like Achilles' heel, the leaf blocked the dragon's blood, allowing the treacherous Hagen to spear him in that exact spot.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Richard Wagner centered his four-opera Ring Cycle (Der Ring des Nibelungen) around him.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sigurd was killed by the dragon Fafnir during their duel.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sigurd killed Fafnir without taking a scratch; his death came years later through political betrayal by his brothers-in-law.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: He rode through a ring of enchanted fire to awaken the sleeping Valkyrie Brynhild.

name: Beowulf
visual_anchor: Towering warrior king in iron chainmail wrestling a monstrous clawed fiend with his bare hands inside a grand wooden mead hall.
core_traits: Legendary Geatish warrior hero and protagonist of the Old English epic poem Beowulf
Possessed the physical hand-grip strength of thirty men
Slew the swamp monster Grendel barehanded by tearing off the beast's arm at Heorot hall
Defeated Grendel's vengeful mother in her underwater lair using an ancient giant-forged sword

facts_and_myths.claim: Beowulf refused to use any weapons or shield when fighting Grendel.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because Grendel fought without weapons, Beowulf deemed it dishonorable to use a blade, relying solely on his bare hands.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Swords were useless anyway, as Grendel had cast a spell bewitching all mortal steel blades.

facts_and_myths.claim: Beowulf died in his youth immediately after defeating Grendel's mother.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Beowulf ruled the Geats peacefully as king for fifty years before dying in old age fighting a fire-breathing dragon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Only his faithful kinsman Wiglaf stayed by his side during his final dragon battle.

name: Grendel
visual_anchor: Grotesque towering swamp monster with matted hair and savage claws emerging from misty fen waters under a pale moonlight.
core_traits: Monstrous humanoid brute terrorizing King Hrothgar's Danish mead hall Heorot
Descendant of the biblical fratricide Cain, cursed to dwell in dark swamps and fens
Raided Heorot nightly for twelve years, slaughtering and devouring sleeping warriors
Mortally wounded when Beowulf ripped off his arm and shoulder in hand-to-hand combat

facts_and_myths.claim: Grendel's skin was impervious to human iron swords and forged weapons.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Grendel laid an enchantment upon every weapon so that no mortal sword could cut his flesh, forcing Beowulf to wrestle him.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hrothgar's warriors hung Grendel's severed arm and claw from the hall rafters as a trophy.

facts_and_myths.claim: Grendel was a dragon that breathed fire over the Danish villages.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Grendel was a giant man-beast living in murky marshes; the fire dragon is a completely separate monster at the end of the epic.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: John Gardner wrote a famous 1971 novel telling the story entirely from Grendel's perspective.

name: Ra
visual_anchor: Falcon-headed deity crowned with a blazing solar disk encircled by the sacred cobra Uraeus, sailing a golden solar boat across sky.
core_traits: Supreme sun god and king of the gods in ancient Egyptian religion
Sails the solar barque Mandjet across the sky by day, bringing light and life to earth
Journeys through the twelve gates of the Underworld (Duat) each night in the barque Mesektet
Battles the primordial giant serpent of chaos Apep (Apophis) every night before sunrise

facts_and_myths.claim: Ra was believed to transform through different forms during the cycle of day: Khepri at dawn, Ra at noon, and Atum at dusk.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Egyptians saw the sun god as the scarab Khepri in the morning, the solar hawk Ra at midday, and the ram-headed Atum at sunset.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Humanity was believed to have been born from the tears of joy shed by Ra's all-seeing Eye.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ra was completely extinguished and died permanently during every solar eclipse.
facts_and_myths.explanation: An eclipse was interpreted as Apep temporarily swallowing Ra's barque, which the gods quickly cut open to restore daylight.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pharaohs claimed the title 'Son of Ra' starting from the Fourth Dynasty.

name: Anubis
visual_anchor: Muscular dark-skinned deity with the sleek head of a black jackal, holding golden scales and an ankh within an ancient stone tomb.
core_traits: Jackal-headed ancient Egyptian god of mummification, embalming, tombs, and the afterlife
Weighs the heart of the deceased against the Feather of Ma'at in the Hall of Two Truths
Depicted with the head of a desert jackal colored pitch black, symbolizing rebirth and fertile Nile soil
Guards tombs from desecration and safely guides departed souls into the Underworld

facts_and_myths.claim: Anubis is colored black not because jackals are black, but because black symbolized rebirth and mummification in Egypt.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Black represented the rich fertile black silt of the Nile and the discoloration of embalmed mummies awaiting rebirth.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Egyptian jackals were actually golden-brown; genetic tests revealed they are actually African golden wolves.

facts_and_myths.claim: Anubis was the ruthless, evil villain of Egyptian mythology who tortured damned souls.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Anubis was a protective, benevolent guardian who ensured fair judgment and preserved mortal bodies for eternal life.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Embalming priests wore wooden jackal masks to embody Anubis during mummification rituals.

name: Osiris
visual_anchor: Mummified king with green skin holding the golden crook and flail, wearing the tall white Atef crown within the Hall of Judgment.
core_traits: Lord of the Underworld, supreme judge of the dead, and god of resurrection and fertility
Portrayed with green skin symbolizing agricultural vegetation and rebirth
Murdered and dismembered into fourteen pieces by his jealous brother Set
Restored to life by his devoted wife Isis and made eternal ruler of the realm of the dead

facts_and_myths.claim: Egyptian farmers associated the annual flooding of the Nile with the resurrection of Osiris.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sprouting crops bursting through black soil symbolized Osiris rising from death to bestow nourishment upon Egypt.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Miniature 'corn mummies' filled with barley and sand were buried to ensure good crop harvests.

facts_and_myths.claim: Osiris was trapped by Set inside a solid gold sarcophagus thrown into the Red Sea.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Set tricked Osiris into lying inside a lavish wooden chest sealed with molten lead and tossed it into the River Nile.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The chest washed ashore in Byblos, Lebanon, where a tamarisk tree enclosed it.

name: Isis
visual_anchor: Graceful goddess spreading magnificent feathered wings in protection, wearing a throne headdress or cow horns holding the solar disk.
core_traits: Supreme goddess of magic, healing, motherhood, protection, and fertility in ancient Egypt
Devoted wife and sister of Osiris and protective mother of Horus
Reassembled the dismembered body of Osiris and performed the first mummification with Anubis
Tricked the sun god Ra into revealing his secret true name to acquire supreme magical power

facts_and_myths.claim: The cult of Isis spread throughout the entire Roman Empire as far north as Britain.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Temples to Isis (Iseums) were built in Pompeii, Rome, and London, making her one of antiquity's most universal deities.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Early Christian iconography of the Virgin Mary holding baby Jesus was heavily influenced by Isis nursing infant Horus.

facts_and_myths.claim: Isis was exclusively worshipped as a goddess of plagues and destruction.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Isis was revered as the supreme healer and nurturer; it was Sekhmet who was associated with divine plagues.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her primary temple was located on the island of Philae in Upper Egypt.

name: Horus
visual_anchor: Regal falcon-headed god wearing the dual red-and-white Pschent crown of Upper and Lower Egypt, carrying a golden spear.
core_traits: Falcon-headed god of the sky, divine kingship, and justice in ancient Egyptian religion
Son of Osiris and Isis who avenged his father's murder in epic contests against his uncle Set
Living Pharaoh was considered the earthly incarnation and physical embodiment of Horus
Lost his left eye in battle against Set, which was restored to become the sacred Eye of Horus (Wedjat)

facts_and_myths.claim: The Eye of Horus was an ancient amulet symbolizing healing, wholeness, protection, and mathematical fractions.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When restored by Thoth, the Eye (Wedjat) represented magical wholeness; its components formed parts of Egyptian hieroglyphic fractions.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sailors painted the Eye of Horus on the bows of ships to ensure safe navigation.

facts_and_myths.claim: Horus was born after his father Osiris had already departed to rule the underworld.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Isis used her supreme magic to posthumously conceive Horus after reviving Osiris's reconstructed body.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His legendary temple at Edfu is one of the best-preserved temples in Egypt.

name: Set
visual_anchor: Lean muscular deity with the head of an enigmatic composite Set beast with curved snout and squared ears, clutching a dark scepter amidst desert sandstorms.
core_traits: God of chaos, violence, deserts, storms, foreigners, and disorder in Egyptian myth
Depicted with the head of the mysterious 'Set animal' with tall squared ears and downturned snout
Jealously assassinated his brother Osiris to usurp the throne of Egypt
Served an essential protective cosmic role defending Ra's solar boat from Apep every night

facts_and_myths.claim: Despite murdering Osiris, Set was honored for nightly saving Ra from the giant serpent Apep.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Set stood at the prow of the sun barge with his copper spear, driving back the chaos serpent Apep when other gods were paralyzed.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Several Nineteenth Dynasty pharaohs took the royal name Seti (man of Set), including Seti I.

facts_and_myths.claim: Set was always depicted as an ordinary domestic dog with floppy ears.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The 'Set animal' (sha) is an enigmatic mythological composite creature featuring squared ears, curved snout, and a stiff forked tail.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Zoologists have debated whether it was based on an aardvark, jackal, saluki hound, or an extinct beast.

name: Bastet
visual_anchor: Graceful cat-headed goddess wearing a patterned linen dress, holding a sacred bronze sistrum rattle and a protective lioness-faced aegis shield.
core_traits: Ancient Egyptian cat goddess of protection, home, domesticity, cats, women, and fertility
Originally worshipped as a fierce lioness warrior before softening into a domestic feline deity
Armed with the sacred musical rattle sistrum to banish negative spirits
Center of worship was the bustling city of Bubastis in the Nile Delta

facts_and_myths.claim: Thousands of mummified cats were buried in sacred catacombs at Bastet's temple in Bubastis.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Excavations at Bubastis uncovered vast cemeteries containing over 300,000 carefully embalmed and wrapped cats as votive offerings.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Killing a cat in ancient Egypt, even accidentally, was punishable by death.

facts_and_myths.claim: Bastet was considered an evil demon that brought bad luck and black magic into homes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bastet was one of Egypt's most beloved and protective household guardians, safeguarding families against diseases and venomous snakes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her annual festival in Bubastis was one of the largest and most joyous celebrations in Egypt.

name: Thoth
visual_anchor: Scholarly deity with the slender curved head of an African sacred ibis, holding a reed scribe pen and papyrus scroll by moonlight.
core_traits: Ibis-headed god of wisdom, writing, mathematics, astronomy, hieroglyphs, and magic
Invented writing and served as the divine scribe recording the judgment of souls in the underworld
Represented by either the sacred curved-beaked ibis bird or the clever baboon
Mediated disputes among gods and maintained the mathematical harmony of the universe

facts_and_myths.claim: The Greeks identified Thoth with their messenger god Hermes, giving rise to Hermes Trismegistus.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Hellenistic Greeks combined Thoth and Hermes into 'Thrice-Great Hermes', the legendary father of alchemy and hermetic philosophy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Thoth was credited with adding five leap days (epagomenal days) to the 360-day calendar by winning moonlight at dice.

facts_and_myths.claim: Thoth could not read or write in Egyptian mythology.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Thoth was the creator of all written words (medu netjer, 'words of the gods') and master of all divine libraries.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ancient Egyptian scribes poured a drop of water as an offering to Thoth before writing.

name: Sobek
visual_anchor: Powerful deity with the ferocious head of a Nile crocodile wearing a plumed sun disk crown, standing proudly beside reed-filled river waters.
core_traits: Crocodile-headed god of the River Nile, fertility, pharaonic potency, and military strength
Associated with the life-giving waters of the Nile and the primal power of the swamp
Worshipped primarily at Kom Ombo and the fertile oasis region of the Faiyum (Crocodilopolis)
Feared and placated to protect fishermen and travelers from deadly crocodile attacks

facts_and_myths.claim: Temples dedicated to Sobek kept sacred living crocodiles adorned with gold earrings and crystal bracelets.
facts_and_myths.explanation: At Crocodilopolis, priests pampered a sacred crocodile named Petsuchos with roast meat and jewels, mummifying it upon death.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Crocodile Museum at Kom Ombo displays dozens of authentic crocodile mummies.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sobek was believed to eat the sun every evening to cause nightfall.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sobek was actually a protector of the sun; in some myths, he rescued the young sons of Horus from the Nile in a lotus net.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sweat from Sobek was mythologically said to have created the waters of the Nile.

name: Sekhmet
visual_anchor: Fierce lioness-headed goddess crowned with a glowing solar disk and rearing uraeus, clad in blood-red robes holding a lotus scepter.
core_traits: Lioness goddess of war, divine vengeance, fire, solar fury, and healing in ancient Egypt
Personification of the destructive burning 'Eye of Ra' sent to punish rebellious mankind
Her fiery breath was believed to create the hot desert winds and infectious plagues
Dual nature: brought plagues when angry, but was also patron goddess of physicians and healing

facts_and_myths.claim: Ra stopped Sekhmet's slaughter of humanity by tricking her into drinking beer dyed red with pomegranate juice.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ra flooded fields with 7,000 jars of red beer; Sekhmet mistook it for human blood, drank greedily, fell asleep, and spared humanity.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: When she awakened peaceful and pacified, she transformed into the gentle goddess Hathor.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sekhmet was depicted as a timid domestic kitten.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sekhmet was always depicted as a fierce African lioness; it was Bastet who took the form of a domestic cat.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over 700 statues of Sekhmet were carved during the reign of Pharaoh Amenhotep III.

name: Hathor
visual_anchor: Serene goddess with graceful cow horns cradling a golden sun disk, holding a sistrum rattle and looking out from a temple courtyard.
core_traits: Beloved ancient Egyptian goddess of joy, music, dance, love, motherhood, and sky
Depicted as a beautiful woman with cow horns and sun disk, or entirely as a sacred maternal cow
Welcomed departed souls into the afterlife with bread, beer, and cool water from the sacred sycamore
Celebrated in grand architectural splendor at the Temple of Dendera

facts_and_myths.claim: Hathor was worshipped as the patron deity of turquoise miners in the Sinai Peninsula.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Egyptians called her 'Lady of Turquoise' and built dedicated rock-cut shrines to her at Serabit el-Khadim in Sinai.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dendera temple features the famous carved 'Dendera Zodiac' ceiling relief.

facts_and_myths.claim: Hathor was the sister and arch-rival of Isis in all Egyptian temple liturgies.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Hathor and Isis shared many attributes and were revered cooperatively; Isis later adopted Hathor's cow-horn headdress.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her sacred mirror was made of polished bronze representing the radiant sun.

name: Anput
visual_anchor: Jackal-headed female deity in ornate pleated linen, crowned with an emblem of a recumbent black jackal atop a standard, walking among tomb shrines.
core_traits: Ancient Egyptian jackal goddess of mummification, funerals, and protection of the deceased
Female counterpart and consort of the jackal god Anubis
Depicted as a woman with a jackal headdress or as a slender female jackal
Primary center of veneration was the seventeenth Upper Egyptian nome of Cynopolis

facts_and_myths.claim: Anput is considered the mother of Kebechet, the goddess of freshness who assists in embalming.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Kebechet was believed to pour purified water and wash the entrails of the deceased during mummification.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her name is simply the feminine grammatical form of Anubis (Anpu + feminine suffix 't').

facts_and_myths.claim: Anput was invented by Greek Ptolemaic rulers and had no presence in the Old Kingdom.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Anput is attested on statues and triad reliefs of Pharaoh Menkaure from the Fourth Dynasty Old Kingdom.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: She protected the body of Osiris during the embalming process alongside Anubis.

name: Ammit
visual_anchor: Fearsome chimera beast with the front of a crocodile, torso of a lion, and hindquarters of a hippopotamus crouching eagerly beside golden scales.
core_traits: Fearsome funerary demoness in the ancient Egyptian Hall of Two Truths
Composite hybrid body combining the three man-eating predators of Egypt: crocodile head, lion body, hippo hindquarters
Sat beside the Scales of Justice while Anubis weighed the deceased's heart against Ma'at's feather
Devoured hearts heavier than the feather of truth, condemning wicked souls to the 'second death' of eternal oblivion

facts_and_myths.claim: Ammit was never worshipped as a goddess in ancient Egyptian temples.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ammit was a terrifying monster to be averted, not revered; no cult temples or regular sacrifices were made to her.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Egyptians placed scarab amulets over the heart to forbid it from testifying against them.

facts_and_myths.claim: If Ammit ate a person's soul, they were sent to burn in a fiery Christian hell.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Consumption by Ammit resulted in total non-existence (uncreation), which Egyptians feared far worse than physical torment.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Souls spared by Ammit entered the blissful reed paradise of Aaru.

name: Apep
visual_anchor: Gigantic abyssal serpent with pitch-black scales and burning sulfurous eyes coiling through the murky subterranean waters of the Duat.
core_traits: Gigantic primordial serpent of chaos, darkness, and non-being in Egyptian mythology
Archenemy of the sun god Ra, dwelling in the dark depths of the underworld Duat
Attempts every single night to swallow the sun barque and plunge the cosmos into eternal darkness
Repelled each morning through the combined strength of Set, Bastet, and divine magic

facts_and_myths.claim: Egyptian priests performed daily rituals chanting the 'Book of Overcoming Apep' to weaken the serpent.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Temple priests crafted wax figurines of Apep, stamped on them, stabbed them, and burned them in fires to magically assist Ra.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Near-Earth asteroid 99942 Apophis was named after this chaos serpent.

facts_and_myths.claim: Apep was slain once and for all by Hercules in ancient times.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Apep can never be permanently destroyed; he must be fought and defeated anew every single night for eternity.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Apep had no eyes or ears, sensing the sun barque solely through vibrations.

name: Bennu
visual_anchor: Graceful giant heron with radiant golden and red plumage and two long crest feathers, perched upon the sacred Benben stone.
core_traits: Sacred ancient Egyptian bird of the sun, creation, renewal, and cyclical rebirth
Depicted as a gray or golden heron with a two-feathered crest wearing the Atef crown
Flew over the primordial waters of Nun at the dawn of creation and landed on the Benben mound
Direct historical and mythological predecessor of the classical Greek Phoenix

facts_and_myths.claim: Greek historian Herodotus's account of the Phoenix was derived from Egyptian tales of the Bennu bird.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Herodotus visited Heliopolis and recorded the Egyptian legend of the sacred Bennu, Hellenizing it into the Phoenix.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Asteroid 101955 Bennu was visited by NASA's OSIRIS-REx sample return mission.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Bennu bird was a mechanical bronze automaton created by Pharaoh Ramesses.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bennu was a sacred living divine animal, identified with an extinct giant heron species (Ardea bennuides).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its cry was said to have initiated the cycle of time at the beginning of the universe.

name: Serket
visual_anchor: Striking goddess wearing a golden dress with a raised-tail golden scorpion perched upon her crown, extending protective arms over a canopic chest.
core_traits: Ancient Egyptian scorpion goddess of protection, medicine, magic, and healing of venom
Depicted as a woman wearing a scorpion on her head, often with its stinger raised in defense
One of the four protective goddesses guarding canopic chests containing mummified internal organs
Invoked to cure venomous bites from scorpions and snakes and protect mothers during childbirth

facts_and_myths.claim: A golden statue of Serket was one of four guardian goddesses discovered in King Tutankhamun's tomb.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Her famous gilded wooden statue stood facing the canopic shrine with arms outstretched to protect the boy king's organs.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her name Serket translates roughly to 'She Who Causes the Throat to Breathe'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Serket was considered the mother of all demonic desert monsters in Egypt.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Serket was a highly benevolent protector who healed mortals and helped bind the chaos serpent Apep.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Priests of Serket in ancient Egypt were specialized physicians treating poisonous stings.

name: Khepri
visual_anchor: Deity in pharaonic kilt whose entire human head is replaced by an iridescent black scarab beetle rolling a glowing golden sun upward.
core_traits: Scarab-headed ancient Egyptian god representing the morning sun, creation, and continuous rebirth
Morning manifestation of the solar deity Ra rising above the eastern horizon
Associated with the sacred dung beetle rolling balls of earth across the ground
Symbol of spontaneous generation and spiritual renewal after death

facts_and_myths.claim: Ancient Egyptians believed scarab beetles were born spontaneously from dung balls without mating.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Observing young beetles emerge from buried brood balls led Egyptians to associate scarabs with self-creation and resurrection.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His name Khepri comes from the verb 'kheper', meaning 'to emerge' or 'to come into being'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Khepri was the Egyptian god of underworld mummification and embalming.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Khepri represented dawn, life, and sunrise; Anubis was the god of mummification.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Winged scarab amulets of Khepri were placed on the chests of mummies to ensure resurrection.

name: Ptah
visual_anchor: Bearded mummiform god with blue skullcap holding a composite scepter of life, stability, and dominion inside a shrine.
core_traits: Ancient Egyptian creator god of Memphis, patron of craftsmen, artisans, sculptors, and builders
Spoke the universe and all living gods into existence through thought in his heart and speech on his tongue
Depicted as a mummified man with green or fair skin holding the combined scepter of Djed, Was, and Ankh
Manifested physically on earth in the form of the sacred Apis bull

facts_and_myths.claim: The English name 'Egypt' originates etymologically from the temple of Ptah at Memphis.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Egyptian name for Memphis was 'Hut-ka-Ptah' (Enclosure of the Ka of Ptah), which Greeks rendered as 'Aigyptos'.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Shabaka Stone preserves the profound theological text known as the Memphite Theology.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ptah was a bloodthirsty warrior deity worshipped only on battlefields.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ptah was a peaceful intellectual creator god celebrated for art, masonry, architecture, and craftsmanship.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Greeks identified Ptah with their blacksmith god Hephaestus.

name: Khonsu
visual_anchor: Youthful mummiform god crowned with a full moon disk resting inside a crescent, holding a crook and flail under a star-filled sky.
core_traits: Ancient Egyptian god of the moon, time, healing, nighttime travelers, and fertility
Son of Amun and Mut, completing the great sacred Theban Triad at Karnak
Depicted as a youthful mummified figure with a sidelock of youth, crowned by crescent and full moon
Believed to possess miraculous powers to heal the sick and banish evil nocturnal demons

facts_and_myths.claim: The Bentresh Stela recounts how a statue of Khonsu was sent to Syria to cure a possessed foreign princess.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The statue of Khonsu the Provider expelled the demon instantly, demonstrating his international reputation for healing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Marvel Comics adapted Khonsu as the divine patron who empowers Moon Knight.

facts_and_myths.claim: Khonsu was the god of the burning midday solar rays.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Khonsu was strictly a lunar deity of the silver moon and nighttime; Ra was the god of midday sun.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His name Khonsu means 'the traveler', describing the moon's nightly journey across the sky.

name: Ankh
visual_anchor: Gleaming golden looped cross emitting sacred divine light, held by pharaohs and gods in ancient carved sandstone reliefs.
core_traits: Sacred ancient Egyptian hieroglyphic symbol representing the concept of eternal life and vitality
Visualized as a cross with a teardrop-shaped loop handle at the top
Held in the hands of Egyptian gods who bestowed the breath of eternal life to pharaohs' nostrils
Ubiquitously worn as a protective magical amulet in life and placed in tombs for the afterlife

facts_and_myths.claim: Coptic Christians in Egypt adopted the ancient Ankh as a Christian cross known as the Crux Ansata.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Early Egyptian Christians recognized the Ankh's symbolism of resurrection and incorporated it into Christian art.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mirrors in ancient Egypt were frequently crafted in the shape of an Ankh, playing on words for mirror and life.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Ankh was an execution weapon used by Egyptian soldiers to defeat enemies.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Ankh was never a weapon; it was an auspicious religious symbol of physical and spiritual vitality.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Tutankhamun's name translates literally to 'Living Image of Amun' (ankh-tut-amun).

name: Scarab Amulet
visual_anchor: Carved green jasper scarab beetle inscribed with hieroglyphic protection spells resting on gold pectorals amidst mummy wrappings.
core_traits: One of the most popular and sacred protective amulets in ancient Egyptian history
Fashioned in the likeness of the dung beetle (Scarabaeus sacer) rolling the solar ball
Heart scarabs were placed over the mummified heart to prevent it from testifying against the deceased
Inscribed on the flat underside with Chapter 30B of the Egyptian Book of the Dead

facts_and_myths.claim: Heart scarabs were inscribed with a direct spell ordering the heart: 'Do not stand up against me as a witness!'
facts_and_myths.explanation: Chapter 30B commanded the heart not to betray its owner when weighed on Anubis's scales in the afterlife.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pharaoh Amenhotep III issued giant commemorative scarabs to announce royal hunts and marriages.

facts_and_myths.claim: In ancient Egypt, scarabs were feared as flesh-eating monsters that swarmed living people.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The 'flesh-eating scarab' trope was invented by Hollywood films like The Mummy; real scarabs were beloved symbols of resurrection.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Scarab amulets were used throughout the Mediterranean as personalized signet rings and seals.

name: Ma'at
visual_anchor: Graceful winged goddess with an ostrich feather standing upright on her head, kneeling with outstretched feathered arms in cosmic harmony.
core_traits: Ancient Egyptian personification of cosmic order, truth, balance, morality, and justice
Depicted as a winged woman wearing a single upright ostrich feather in her headband
Her sacred feather of truth served as the counterweight against which human hearts were weighed
Pharaohs had a sacred religious duty to maintain Ma'at and banish Isfet (chaos and falsehood)

facts_and_myths.claim: Ancient Egyptian judges wore a small golden emblem of Ma'at as a pendant of impartiality.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The chief vizier and high judges wore a lapis lazuli or gold figure of Ma'at around their necks while presiding over trials.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The 42 Negative Confessions declared before Ma'at's court included 'I have not stolen' and 'I have not polluted water'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ma'at was an aggressive goddess of vengeance who struck down mortals with lightning.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ma'at was the serene, eternal cosmic principle of harmonious balance rather than a punitive warrior deity.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Without Ma'at, the Egyptians believed the universe would dissolve into chaotic nothingness.

name: Taweret
visual_anchor: Benevolent pregnant bipedal hippopotamus goddess with crocodile tail and lion paws, leaning resting paws on the protective Sa knot.
core_traits: Ancient Egyptian protective goddess of childbirth, pregnancy, fertility, and mothers
Depicted as a bipedal pregnant hippopotamus with lion paws, human breasts, and crocodile back/tail
Carries the sacred Sa knot of protection and an ivory wand to ward off malignant spirits from nurseries
Fierce maternal deity whose ferocious appearance terrified malevolent demons away from infants

facts_and_myths.claim: Egyptian women used curved hippopotamus ivory wands inscribed with Taweret to draw magical protection circles around newborn beds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Apotropaic ivory birth tusks featuring Taweret and Bes were swept across the floor to repel evil spirits and snakes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her constellation was identified with the northern celestial sky near Ursa Major.

facts_and_myths.claim: Taweret was an evil river monster worshipped only by bandits and tomb robbers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Taweret was one of the most widely beloved domestic deities in ordinary Egyptian homes across all social classes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Vessels shaped like Taweret had holes in the nipples to pour milk for infants.

name: Hapi
visual_anchor: Blue-skinned androgynous deity with a large belly, carrying overflowing trays of lotus blossoms, papyrus, and fish from the Nile.
core_traits: Ancient Egyptian god of the annual fertility-bringing inundation of the River Nile
Portrayed as an androgynous figure with a rounded belly and nourishing breasts, symbolizing abundant harvests
Often depicted in twin aspects: Hapi of Upper Egypt wearing lotus plants and Hapi of Lower Egypt wearing papyrus
Believed to dwell in an underground cavern near Elephantine Island at Aswan

facts_and_myths.claim: Pharaohs threw hymns, food, and amulets into the Nile to ensure Hapi brought the flood at the right level.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The 'Hymn to Hapi' praised the floodwaters; a flood that was too high caused destruction, while too low meant famine.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His blue or green skin symbolized the refreshing waters and fertile vegetation.

facts_and_myths.claim: Hapi was the same deity as Hapi the son of Horus who guarded the lungs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Hapi the Nile flood god was distinct from Hapy, the baboon-headed son of Horus guarding the lungs in canopic jars.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Statues show dual figures of Hapi tying lotus and papyrus stems together (the sema-tawy motif).

name: Neith
visual_anchor: Ancient warrior goddess wearing the red Deshret crown of Lower Egypt, holding a bow and two crossed arrows with regal authority.
core_traits: One of Egypt's oldest primordial creator goddesses and deity of hunting, warfare, and weaving
Depicted wearing the Red Crown of Lower Egypt and holding crossed arrows and a shield
Worshipped at Sais in the western Nile Delta since predynastic times
Considered an uncreated primeval mother who wove the cosmos on her divine loom

facts_and_myths.claim: Greek philosophers including Plato explicitly identified the Egyptian goddess Neith with Athena.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In Timaeus, Plato notes that the citizens of Sais revere Neith, whom they consider identical to Greek Athena.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her temple at Sais bore the inscription: 'I am all that has been, and is, and shall be, and my robe no mortal has yet unveiled'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Neith was exclusively a goddess of domestic cooking with no connection to weapons.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Neith was foremost a warrior and huntress whose sacred emblem consisted of two crossed arrows on an animal shield.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: She was summoned as supreme arbiter in the dispute between Horus and Set.

name: Bes
visual_anchor: Stout, bearded lion-faced dwarf deity with sticking-out tongue and feather headdress, banging a tambourine to scare away evil spirits.
core_traits: Beloved ancient Egyptian household deity protecting mothers, infants, sleep, and families
Depicted as a lion-featured dwarf sticking out his tongue, wearing a feathered crown and leopard skin
Rarely shown in profile; unusually depicted full-face in Egyptian art to confront evil head-on
Danced, made funny faces, and played drums to scare away nightmares, scorpions, and demons

facts_and_myths.claim: Bes was one of the few Egyptian gods depicted full-face facing forward rather than in profile.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Almost all Egyptian art used profile view; Bes looked outward directly at viewers to intimidate demons and protect doorways.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mothers painted Bes on their bodies during labor to ensure safe child delivery.

facts_and_myths.claim: Bes was a somber funeral god who accompanied pharaohs to tomb chambers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bes was a festive, comic god of everyday domestic life, music, dancing, humor, and joy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His image was carved onto makeup jars, mirrors, and bed headboards.

name: Wadjet
visual_anchor: Rearing golden Egyptian cobra with expanded hood, perched atop the pharaonic crown spitting blinding fire at enemies.
core_traits: Predynastic protective cobra goddess and patron deity of Lower Egypt
Manifested as the sacred Uraeus cobra rearing up on the crowns of pharaohs and gods
Spit burning venom and fire to defend the monarch against all enemies
Paired with the vulture goddess Nekhbet as the 'Two Ladies' (Nebty) of unified Egypt

facts_and_myths.claim: The rearing cobra on Tutankhamun's famous gold burial mask depicts the goddess Wadjet.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The mask features both the cobra Wadjet and the vulture Nekhbet on the forehead, symbolizing dominion over unified Egypt.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her sacred city was Buto in the Nile Delta, known for its oracle.

facts_and_myths.claim: Wadjet was a malevolent snake demon who plotted to overthrow Egyptian kings.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Wadjet was the supreme royal protectress who served as the king's personal fiery shield.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Papyrus swamps were sacred to her, and she hid baby Horus from Set in the marshes of Chemmis.

name: Nekhbet
visual_anchor: Majestic white vulture with immense outstretched wings hovering protectively over the pharaoh, clutching a shen ring of eternity in talons.
core_traits: Ancient Egyptian vulture goddess and supreme patron deity of Upper Egypt
Depicted as a white griffon vulture with wings spread in protective embrace over the pharaoh
Holds the Shen ring of eternal protection in her claws
Paired with Wadjet the cobra as the dual protective emblems on royal crowns

facts_and_myths.claim: Egyptian queens often wore elaborate gold vulture headdresses honoring Nekhbet.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Queens like Nefertiti and Cleopatra wore crowns modeled on Nekhbet's body and wings draped over their hair.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her cult center was the ancient city of Nekheb (modern Elkab) in Upper Egypt.

facts_and_myths.claim: Vultures were viewed by ancient Egyptians as disgusting, unclean creatures.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Egyptians revered vultures as symbols of motherhood and protection due to their dedicated care for their chicks.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The hieroglyph for 'mother' (mwt) was written using the image of a vulture.

name: Imhotep
visual_anchor: Deified Egyptian sage seated in a linen kilt with shaved head, unrolling an architectural papyrus blueprint on his lap.
core_traits: Historic genius polymath, royal architect to Pharaoh Djoser, and pioneer of stone architecture
Designed the revolutionary Step Pyramid of Djoser at Saqqara, the world's first colossal stone building
Deified 2,000 years after his death as the god of medicine, healing, and architecture
Equated by Hellenistic Greeks with Asclepius, the Greek god of medicine

facts_and_myths.claim: Imhotep is one of the only historical mortal non-royals ever deified into a full god in Egyptian history.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Along with Amenhotep son of Hapu, Imhotep achieved full divine status with temples and cult worship across Egypt.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His lost tomb at Saqqara remains one of Egyptology's greatest undiscovered holy grails.

facts_and_myths.claim: Imhotep was a cursed high priest who was mummified alive as portrayed in Hollywood movies.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The 1932 and 1999 films The Mummy fictionalized Imhotep as a villain; historical Imhotep was a celebrated, revered genius.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: He served as vizier, high priest of Ra at Heliopolis, and royal physician.

name: Cleopatra
visual_anchor: Charismatic queen wearing a gold royal diadem and pleated royal garments, holding a golden asp amidst silk canopies on a royal barge.
core_traits: Last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt, legendary for intellect, charisma, and diplomacy
Presented herself to subjects as the living terrestrial incarnation of the goddess Isis (Nea Isis)
Formed fateful romantic and political alliances with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony
Immortalized in legend for choosing death by venomous asp rather than submission to Octavian

facts_and_myths.claim: Cleopatra was the only Ptolemaic ruler who learned to speak the native Egyptian language.
facts_and_myths.explanation: While her Greek dynasty spoke Koine Greek for 300 years, Cleopatra was polyglot and fluently spoke Egyptian and several other tongues.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Plutarch recorded that her true charm lay in her sparkling intellect, wit, and melodious voice rather than beauty alone.

facts_and_myths.claim: Cleopatra was an ethnic Egyptian born to peasant lineage.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cleopatra was of Macedonian Greek ancestry, descending directly from Alexander the Great's general Ptolemy I Soter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: She minted coins bearing her likeness and ruled jointly with her sons.

name: Sun Wukong
visual_anchor: Defiant agile monkey warrior clad in golden chainmail and phoenix-feather cap, spinning a glowing red-and-gold compliant staff on a somersault cloud.
core_traits: Legendary mythical stone-born monkey hero of the Chinese classic Journey to the West
Possesses superhuman strength, 72 earthly transformations, and leaps 108,000 li on a cloud
Wields the As-You-Will Gold-Banded Cudgel (Ruyi Jingu Bang) weighing 13,500 pounds
Achieved multiple layers of immortality by erasing his name from the Book of Life and Death and eating immortal peaches

facts_and_myths.claim: Sun Wukong was trapped beneath the Five Elements Mountain for 500 years by the Buddha.
facts_and_myths.explanation: After wreaking havoc in Heaven, the Buddha pinned Wukong under the mountain with a sacred mantra seal until Tang Sanzang freed him.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His magical golden staff was originally an ocean anchor used by Yu the Great to measure floodwaters.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sun Wukong was defeated easily by the Jade Emperor's personal soldiers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The heavenly hosts of 100,000 soldiers could not defeat Wukong; only the Buddha was able to subdue him.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dragon Ball's protagonist Son Goku was directly inspired by Sun Wukong.

name: Jade Emperor
visual_anchor: Venerable celestial sovereign with long beard and beaded imperial headdress seated upon an ornate dragon throne in a palatial cloud temple.
core_traits: Supreme monarch of Heaven and ruler of all realms in Chinese folk religion and Taoism
Commands the celestial bureaucracy, governing gods, spirits, and mortal affairs
Organized the legendary Great Race of animals that established the twelve signs of the Chinese Zodiac
Resides in the Palace of Heavenly Purity surrounded by immortal courtiers

facts_and_myths.claim: The Jade Emperor selected the twelve zodiac animals through a race across a wide river.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In legend, the Jade Emperor declared that the order of years in the calendar would be determined by the order animals crossed the river.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The rat won first place by riding on the ox's back and jumping off at the finish line.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Jade Emperor was born as an evil demon who conquered Heaven through dark magic.
facts_and_myths.explanation: He cultivated virtue, benevolence, and Taoist self-perfection over millions of eons before ascending to the throne.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: On his birthday, families burn joss paper and offer sweet foods across Asia.

name: Nezha
visual_anchor: Spirited boy warrior balancing atop two flaming Wind-Fire Wheels, wielding the Fire-Tipped Spear and Universe Ring wrapped in a red silk sash.
core_traits: Boy warrior deity and protection hero in Chinese mythology and the classic Investiture of the Gods
Born as a ball of flesh after a three-and-a-half-year pregnancy and sliced open by his father Li Jing
Flies at incredible speeds upon his twin flaming Wind-Fire Wheels
Reincarnated by master Taiyi Zhenren with a body fashioned from lotus roots and leaves

facts_and_myths.claim: Nezha sliced his own flesh and carved his bones to return them to his parents after battling the Dragon King.
facts_and_myths.explanation: To save his family and town from the Dragon Kings' flooding wrath, Nezha committed filial suicide and returned his body to his parents.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His mentor Taiyi Zhenren resurrected him with an immortal body made of lotus flowers.

facts_and_myths.claim: Nezha's signature weapon was a giant iron club forged by dwarves.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Nezha wields the Fire-Tipped Spear, the Universe Ring (Qiankun Quan), and the red Armillary Sash (Huntian Ling).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Nezha is widely worshipped as the patron god of truck, bus, and taxi drivers in Taiwan.

name: Erlang Shen
visual_anchor: Noble celestial warrior in silver armor with a vertical third eye glowing on his forehead, wielding a three-pointed double-edged blade beside a celestial hound.
core_traits: Mighty three-eyed celestial warrior god in Chinese mythology and folklore
Possesses a vertical truth-seeing third eye in his forehead that penetrates all illusions and shapeshifters
Accompanied in battle by his faithful divine hunting companion, the Howling Celestial Dog (Xiaotian Quan)
Master of 72 earthly transformations who fought Sun Wukong to a standstill

facts_and_myths.claim: Erlang Shen successfully captured Sun Wukong when all other heavenly generals failed.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Using his third eye to counter Wukong's transformations and assisted by his hound and Laozi's diamond ring, Erlang captured the monkey king.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: He is the nephew of the Jade Emperor through the emperor's mortal sister Yaoji.

facts_and_myths.claim: Erlang Shen's third eye was a physical wound inflicted by an arrow.
facts_and_myths.explanation: His third eye is a divine organ of celestial perception capable of discerning truth from falsehood across all realms.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His weapon is the unique Three-Pointed, Double-Edged Spear.

name: Nine-Tailed Fox
visual_anchor: Mystical white fox with nine billowing bushy tails sitting on an enchanted shrine stone beneath cherry blossoms under a full moon.
core_traits: Mythical shapeshifting fox spirit appearing across East Asian folklore (China, Japan, Korea)
Grows an additional tail every century of cultivation until reaching nine tails at one thousand years
Capable of shapeshifting into a breathtakingly beautiful woman to enchant or deceive mortals
Possesses fox-fire (kitsunebi), immense illusions, and spiritual immortality

facts_and_myths.claim: In Japanese Shinto tradition, white foxes (kitsune) serve as holy messengers of Inari, the god of rice.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Kitsune statues holding keys to granaries or jewels in their mouths guard thousands of Inari shrines across Japan.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Fried tofu pouches (inarizushi) are considered the favorite snack of sacred shrine foxes.

facts_and_myths.claim: In Korean folklore, the Gumiho is a benevolent vegetarian spirit that protects villages.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Korean Gumiho lore portrays the fox as a sinister predator that consumes human livers or hearts to achieve full human form.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The nine-tailed fox inspired Naruto's Kurama and Pokemon's Ninetales.

name: Tanuki
visual_anchor: Chubby jolly raccoon dog standing upright wearing a straw hat, carrying a ceramic sake flask and promissory note outside a traditional tavern.
core_traits: Mischievous shape-shifting yokai based on the Japanese raccoon dog (Nyctereutes viverrinus)
Depicted with a prominent round belly, straw traveler hat, sake bottle, and empty promissory note
Master of illusions, turning leaves into fake gold coins and shapeshifting into teapots and humans
Symbol of good fortune, conviviality, prosperity, and playful humor throughout Japan

facts_and_myths.claim: Ceramic statues of tanuki are placed outside restaurants and bars across Japan to welcome customers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Shigaraki pottery tanuki with eight lucky attributes (including big eyes, sake flask, and smile) are classic Japanese business emblems.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The famous folk tale 'Bunbuku Chagama' tells of a grateful tanuki that disguised itself as a singing tea kettle.

facts_and_myths.claim: Tanuki and North American raccoons are the exact same biological species.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The tanuki is a canid (related to dogs and foxes), while raccoons belong to the procyonid family.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mario's Tanooki Suit in Super Mario Bros. 3 allows him to fly and turn into a stone statue.

name: Tengu
visual_anchor: Red-faced humanoid mountain ascetic with an exceptionally long prominent nose, wearing black wings and holding a feather fan (hauchiwa).
core_traits: Legendary mountain-dwelling yokai and guardian spirits in Japanese Shinto and Buddhist lore
Depicted either as bird-men with crow beaks (Karasu Tengu) or red-faced men with long noses (Daitengu)
Dress as yamabushi mountain ascetic monks and wield magical feather fans to control fierce winds
Famed as supreme masters of martial arts and swordsmanship who tutored the hero Minamoto no Yoshitsune

facts_and_myths.claim: The legendary Japanese swordsman Minamoto no Yoshitsune was said to have learned fencing from the Tengu king Sojobo.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Folklore recounts that Yoshitsune trained secretly at night on Mount Kurama under the guidance of the Tengu master.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Tengu's fan (hauchiwa) was believed capable of blowing away entire armies.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Japanese name 'Tengu' translates literally to 'Heavenly Dog', originally derived from Chinese Tiangou meteors.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The characters for Tengu literally read 'heavenly dog', tracing back to falling meteorites likened to barking celestial dogs in China.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over centuries in Japan, the creature evolved into an avian mountain spirit rather than a dog.

name: Kappa
visual_anchor: Child-sized reptilian water creature with green scaly skin, turtle carapace on its back, webbed hands, and a water-filled dish atop its head.
core_traits: Amphibious humanoid yokai inhabiting the rivers, ponds, and lakes of Japan
Possesses a turtle shell, webbed hands and feet, beak-like mouth, and a hollow water-filled dish (sara) on its head
If the dish on its head loses its water, the kappa becomes paralyzed and loses all strength
Infamous for pulling animals and children underwater, wrestling sumo, and an obsession with cucumbers

facts_and_myths.claim: A person can defeat a Kappa by bowing deeply, causing the water in its head dish to spill.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Kappa are obsessed with polite etiquette; when bowed to, they bow back, spilling their vital water and rendering them helpless.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Cucumber sushi rolls are called 'kappa maki' in Japan because cucumbers are the Kappa's favorite food.

facts_and_myths.claim: Kappa were harmless fluffy woodland creatures that lived high in cedar trees.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Kappa were dangerous aquatic predators feared for extracting the mythical 'shirikodama' ball from victims' bodies.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Once befriended, Kappa are honorable and skilled at bone-setting medicine.

name: Oni
visual_anchor: Towering red-skinned ogre with two sharp horns, tusks protruding from its jaw, wearing a tiger-skin loincloth and brandishing an iron club.
core_traits: Monstrous horned ogre or demon of Japanese folklore and Buddhist hell (Jigoku)
Depicted with red, blue, or green skin, two horns, wild hair, and fangs
Wears a tiger-skin loincloth and wields a heavy studded iron war club (kanabo)
Ward of evil ceremonies at Setsubun, where people throw roasted soybeans shouting 'Demons out! Luck in!'

facts_and_myths.claim: The Japanese idiom 'an oni with an iron club' (oni-ni-kanabo) means making someone who is already strong invincible.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because the Oni is already supernaturally strong, giving it an iron club represents an unbeatable advantage.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: At the Setsubun festival in February, children throw roasted beans to banish Oni from homes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Oni were depicted as miniature winged fairies that granted good dreams.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Oni were brutal giant human-eaters and tormentors of wicked souls in Buddhist underworld realms.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Traditional Japanese roofs feature oni-faced tiles (onigawara) to ward off evil spirits.

name: Yuki-Onna
visual_anchor: Inhumanly pale, breathtakingly beautiful woman in a flowing white kimono drifting soundlessly through a howling blizzard in a snowy forest.
core_traits: Ethereal spirit or yokai of winter and snow in Japanese folklore
Appears on freezing blizzard nights as a beautiful maiden with snow-white skin and piercing eyes
Floats effortlessly above the snow leaving no footprints behind
Can freeze travelers solid with her icy breath or lead lost souls astray into frozen mountain peaks

facts_and_myths.claim: In Lafcadio Hearn's famous tale, Yuki-Onna spared a young woodcutter on condition that he never tell anyone he saw her.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Years later, the woodcutter casually mentioned the event to his wife, who revealed herself as Yuki-Onna and vanished into mist.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: She spared him only because of their children, leaving him with a warning to care for them.

facts_and_myths.claim: Yuki-Onna loves bathing in boiling volcanic hot springs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Heat melts her completely; hot water or intense warmth dissolves her into a puddle of cold water or white vapor.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her legends are particularly prevalent in Tohoku and Niigata prefectures.

name: Dragon King
aliases: Dragon King of the East Sea
visual_anchor: Regal crowned dragon monarch wearing imperial silk robes, seated upon a coral throne in an underwater crystal palace surrounded by sea creatures.
core_traits: Divine ruler of the water and weather in Chinese mythology and Taoism
Four Dragon Kings govern the four seas corresponding to the cardinal directions (Ao Guang rules the East Sea)
Commands all marine life and controls clouds, rain, typhoons, and floods
Resides in an opulent underwater Crystal Palace filled with coral, pearls, and mythical treasures

facts_and_myths.claim: Sun Wukong visited the Dragon King Ao Guang to obtain his famous compliant golden staff.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ao Guang tried to give Wukong heavy weapons, but Wukong chose the 13,500-pound pillar that held down the ocean palace.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Wukong also demanded and received magical golden chainmail and cloud-walking shoes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Eastern Dragon Kings breathe fire and burn down cities.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Asian dragons are water deities associated with rain, rivers, and benevolence, having no desire to breathe fire.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In times of drought, ancient Chinese villages paraded statues of the Dragon King to pray for rain.

name: Garuda
visual_anchor: Colossal divine bird-man with golden eagle wings, curved beak, and muscular human torso soaring across a brilliant azure sky clutching serpents.
core_traits: Divine bird king and mount (vahana) of the supreme god Vishnu in Hindu and Buddhist mythology
Depicted with the head, wings, and talons of an eagle and the torso of a muscular human
Eternal sworn archenemy of the serpentine Nagas, whom he hunts and feeds upon
Official national symbol of both Thailand (Phra Khrut Pha) and Indonesia (Garuda Pancasila)

facts_and_myths.claim: Garuda is the official national coat of arms of both Thailand and Indonesia.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Thailand uses Garuda as its royal and state emblem, and Indonesia features the golden Garuda on its national coat of arms.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Indonesia's national airline is named Garuda Indonesia.

facts_and_myths.claim: Garuda stole the nectar of immortality (Amrita) from the gods to ransom his captive mother.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Garuda defeated the gods and secured the Amrita to free his mother Vinata from the serpent queen Kadru.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Vishnu was so impressed by Garuda's integrity that he granted him immortality without drinking the nectar.

name: Naga
visual_anchor: Majestic multi-headed giant king cobra with flared golden hood, coiled protectively around an ancient stone temple staircase above a lotus lake.
core_traits: Semi-divine serpentine beings in Hinduism, Buddhism, and Southeast Asian folklore
Inhabit underground watery kingdoms, subterranean palaces, rivers, and lakes
Often depicted with multiple heads (typically five, seven, or nine) with flared cobra hoods
Protectors of sacred waters, hidden treasures, fertility, and Buddhist dharma

facts_and_myths.claim: The Naga king Mucalinda sheltered the meditating Buddha from a severe week-long storm with his multi-headed hood.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When heavy rain threatened the meditating Buddha at Bodh Gaya, Mucalinda coiled beneath him and spread his giant hood as an umbrella.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Naga balustrades line the grand entrances of Angkor Wat in Cambodia.

facts_and_myths.claim: Nagas and Garudas lived in peaceful brotherhood without ever fighting.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Nagas and the giant bird Garuda are mythological mortal enemies, constantly locked in celestial predation.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The female equivalent is called a Nagini.

name: Qilin
visual_anchor: Luminous chimerical beast with dragon head, antlers, carp scales, and cloven deer hooves walking gently upon clouds without bending grass.
core_traits: Mythical hooved chimerical creature in Chinese and East Asian mythology symbolizing serenity and good fortune
Combines dragon head, antlers, scaled body, ox tail, and cloven horse hooves
So gentle that it steps so lightly it avoids harming a single blade of grass or tiny insect
Said to appear only during the reign of an exceptionally benevolent ruler or the birth of a sage

facts_and_myths.claim: A Qilin was prophesied to have appeared just before the birth of the philosopher Confucius.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Legend states a Qilin appeared to Confucius's mother, coughing up a jade tablet predicting the birth of an uncrowned king.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: When Ming admiral Zheng He brought real African giraffes to China in 1414, the court hailed them as real Qilins.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Qilin was a vicious carnivore that hunted human travelers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Qilin is the epitome of non-violence and mercy, refusing even to eat live plants or tread on insects.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The famous Japanese Kirin Brewery displays a stylized Kirin on its beer labels.

name: Jiangshi
visual_anchor: Rigid corpse dressed in dark Qing dynasty official robes with arms outstretched, hopping down a misty forest path with a yellow paper talisman on its forehead.
core_traits: Reanimated corpse in Chinese folklore that moves exclusively by hopping with arms held stiffly forward
Rigor mortis prevents its joints from bending, requiring it to hop forward to move
Absorbs the life essence (qi) of living victims, typically at night
Subdued by sticking a yellow paper talisman (fulu) inscribed with Taoist spells on its forehead

facts_and_myths.claim: The Jiangshi legend arose from Taoist priests transporting dead laborers home for burial by carrying them on bamboo poles.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Corpses tied upright to bouncing bamboo poles carried by two priests appeared to hop rhythmically through nighttime mists.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sticky glutinous rice (glutinous rice) is traditionally believed to repel or cure Jiangshi bites.

facts_and_myths.claim: Jiangshi are harmed by silver crosses and garlic cloves.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Crosses and garlic are European vampire tropes; Jiangshi are countered by peach-wood swords, mirrors, rooster crows, and Taoist talismans.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The 1985 Hong Kong comedy horror film Mr. Vampire popularized the creature globally.

name: Guan Yu
visual_anchor: Imposing red-faced warrior general with a long sweeping black beard, green dragon robes, and the Green Dragon Crescent Blade halberd.
core_traits: Historic general of the Three Kingdoms period deified as the god of war, loyalty, justice, and righteousness
Famed protagonist of Romance of the Three Kingdoms alongside his sworn brothers Liu Bei and Zhang Fei
Wielded the legendary heavy Green Dragon Crescent Blade (Guandao) and rode the Red Hare steed
Worshipped by police officers, martial artists, businessmen, and triad members alike for loyalty and integrity

facts_and_myths.claim: Shrines dedicated to Guan Yu are placed inside police stations and businesses throughout Hong Kong and Taiwan.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because he represents unshakeable loyalty, righteousness, and courage, both law enforcement and merchants revere him.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Unlike Ares, Guan Yu is worshipped not for bloodlust, but for unwavering code of honor and moral discipline.

facts_and_myths.claim: Guan Yu was purely a fictional character invented in Ming Dynasty novels.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Guan Yu was a real historical military general who died in 220 AD, subsequently elevated by successive emperors.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: He was posthumously granted the title 'Holy Emperor Lord Guan' (Guan Sheng Di Jun).

name: Chang'e
visual_anchor: Ethereal goddess in flowing silk robes floating gracefully upward toward the luminous full moon above the clouds, cradling a white rabbit.
core_traits: Chinese goddess of the moon and central figure of the annual Mid-Autumn Festival
Wife of the legendary master divine archer Hou Yi who shot down nine scorching suns
Drank the elixir of immortality given by the Queen Mother of the West and floated up to the moon
Resides in the Moon Palace (Guanghan Gong) accompanied only by the Jade Rabbit and woodcutter Wu Gang

facts_and_myths.claim: China's lunar exploration spacecraft program was officially named 'Chang'e' after the moon goddess.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The CNSA Chang'e lunar exploration missions, including Chang'e 4 (first far-side landing), honor her legend.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The lunar rover deployed was named Yutu (Jade Rabbit).

facts_and_myths.claim: During the Mid-Autumn Festival, people eat mooncakes while gazing at the full moon to honor Chang'e.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Families gather under the full autumn moon, sharing sweet round mooncakes symbolizing family reunion and completeness.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The osmanthus tree in her lunar palace can never be felled, instantly healing each axe blow.

name: Jade Rabbit
visual_anchor: Snow-white rabbit standing on its hind legs pounding a pestle into a stone mortar of glowing celestial elixir on the cratered moon.
core_traits: Mythical hare residing on the moon in East Asian folklore (China, Japan, Korea)
Faithful companion of the moon goddess Chang'e in her lunar palace
In Chinese tradition, it tirelessly pounds the elixir of immortality in a stone mortar
In Japanese and Korean folklore, it pounds sticky sweet mochi / rice cakes instead of medicine

facts_and_myths.claim: The Moon Rabbit legend arose from human pareidolia seeing the dark craters (maria) on the full moon as a rabbit.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Across Asian cultures, dark markings on the moon resemble a rabbit leaning over a mortar and pestle.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Apollo 11 astronauts were told by Houston ground control to keep an eye out for 'a lovely girl with a big rabbit' on the moon.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Jade Rabbit was a ferocious predatory hare that hunted dragons on the moon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Jade Rabbit was honored for selflessness; in Buddhist Jataka tales, the hare offered its own body as food for a hungry beggar.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Touched by the hare's sacrifice, the deity Indra drew its likeness on the face of the moon.

name: King Arthur
visual_anchor: Noble armored monarch wearing a golden crown, drawing the glowing sword Excalibur from a mystical lake beneath a fluttering red dragon banner.
core_traits: Legendary British monarch who established the peaceful kingdom of Camelot and the Round Table
Proved his divine right to kingship by pulling the sword from the stone
Gifted the enchanted blade Excalibur and its wound-preventing scabbard by the Lady of the Lake
Fostered the chivalric fellowship of the Knights of the Round Table in search of the Holy Grail

facts_and_myths.claim: The 'Sword in the Stone' and 'Excalibur' are often two completely different swords in original medieval romances.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The sword pulled from the anvil broke in battle; Merlin subsequently led Arthur to the Lady of the Lake to receive Excalibur.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: His legendary scabbard possessed the magical power to prevent the wearer from losing blood.

facts_and_myths.claim: Clear contemporary 6th-century archaeological proof exists showing Arthur built Camelot as an stone concentric castle.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Arthur is a composite legendary figure; concentric stone castles did not exist in Britain until centuries after the sub-Roman era.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Legend says he sleeps in the magical isle of Avalon, fated to return when Britain needs him most.

name: Merlin
visual_anchor: Wise silver-bearded wizard in star-embroidered indigo robes holding an ancient wooden staff, summoning glowing blue wisps of arcane magic.
core_traits: Legendary wizard, prophet, seer, and chief counselor to King Arthur and Uther Pendragon
Born as the son of an incubus demon and a mortal virtuous nun, giving him supernatural powers
Orchestrated the sword in the stone test and guided Arthur through his royal reign
Archetype of the wise wizard in Western literature, inspiring characters like Gandalf and Dumbledore

facts_and_myths.claim: In Geoffrey of Monmouth's chronicle, Merlin magically transported the giant stones of Stonehenge from Ireland to Salisbury Plain.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Geoffrey claimed Merlin used magical machines to dismantle the 'Giant's Dance' circle in Ireland and re-erect it in England.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Stonehenge actually predates Arthurian legends by thousands of years.

facts_and_myths.claim: Merlin was killed in battle by King Arthur's sword Excalibur.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Merlin was enchanted and trapped inside a hawthorn tree or glass tower by his student Viviane (the Lady of the Lake).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: He was said to age backward, remembering the future but forgetting the past.

name: Morgan le Fay
visual_anchor: Enigmatic dark-haired sorceress in velvet emerald robes holding a glowing scrying orb inside a candlelit stone tower chamber.
core_traits: Powerful sorceress and half-sister of King Arthur in Arthurian romance
Trained in the magical and healing arts by the arch-mage Merlin
Evolved in medieval literature from a benevolent magical healer into a dangerous rival and antagonist to Arthur's court
One of the mystical queens who transports mortally wounded Arthur to the enchanted isle of Avalon

facts_and_myths.claim: In the earliest 12th-century Arthurian texts, Morgan was depicted as a noble, benevolent fairy healer.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In Geoffrey of Monmouth's Vita Merlini, she is the wise ruler of Avalon who lovingly treats Arthur's mortal battle wounds.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Later Christian romances recast her as an incestuous villain to contrast with chivalric ideals.

facts_and_myths.claim: The optical mirage phenomenon 'Fata Morgana' in the Strait of Messina is named after Morgan le Fay.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Italian sailors believed the towering castles seen hovering over the water were fairy illusions conjured by Morgan (Fata Morgana).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: She attempted to steal Excalibur's protective scabbard to give to her lover Sir Accolon.

name: Lady of the Lake
visual_anchor: Ethereal mystical woman emerging gracefully from mist over a glass-calm lake, holding up the gleaming jeweled hilt of Excalibur.
core_traits: Mystical water enchantress in Arthurian legend residing in an otherworldly realm beneath a magical lake
Bestowed the divine sword Excalibur and its enchanted scabbard upon young King Arthur
Raised Sir Lancelot du Lac from childhood in her enchanted palace after his father's death
Reclaimed Excalibur when Sir Bedivere threw the blade back into the waters upon Arthur's demise

facts_and_myths.claim: When Bedivere threw Excalibur into the lake, a hand emerged from the water, caught the sword, brandished it three times, and vanished.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sir Thomas Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur dramatically recounts the Lady of the Lake's hand catching Excalibur before sinking below.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bedivere tried to hide the sword twice before finally obeying Arthur's dying command.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Lady of the Lake was an evil swamp hag who drowned passing knights.
facts_and_myths.explanation: She was a high fairy queen associated with divine protection, healing, and chivalric destiny.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: She famously imprisoned Merlin in an enchanted rock or tree using his own spells.

name: Banshee
visual_anchor: Spectral gaunt woman with wild silver hair and blood-red eyes clad in a tattered gray shroud, wailing mournfully beside a desolate Celtic bog.
core_traits: Female spirit in Irish folklore whose mournful shrieking or keening heralds an impending death in a family
Tied traditionally to the five major historic Irish Gaelic royal families (O'Neill, O'Brien, O'Connor, O'Grady, Kavanagh)
Appears in three guises: a beautiful young maiden, a stately matron, or a ragged haggard crone
Often seen washing blood-stained clothes or funeral shrouds in a river (the Bean-Nighe)

facts_and_myths.claim: The Irish term 'Bean Sidhe' translates literally to 'Woman of the Fairy Mound'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In Gaelic, 'bean' means woman and 'sidhe' refers to the ancient burial mounds where fairy folk dwell.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her wailing (keening) reflects the traditional Irish custom of women singing lamentations at wakes.

facts_and_myths.claim: A Banshee directly kills people by attacking them with razor-sharp claws.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Banshee never causes death; she is merely a mournful prophet warning the family of approaching tragedy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Legend says that if you find her silver comb on the ground, you should never pick it up.

name: Leprechaun
visual_anchor: Mischievous little bearded fairy man in an emerald coat and buckle hat, tapping a tiny leather shoe on a toadstool beside a pot of gold.
core_traits: Diminutive solitary fairy of Irish folklore, traditionally working as a shoemaker for the Tuatha De Danann
Famed for guarding a hidden pot of gold buried at the end of the rainbow
Master of trickery; if captured by a mortal, will grant three wishes in exchange for freedom
Will vanish instantly if the captor takes their eyes off him for even a single fraction of a second

facts_and_myths.claim: In original Irish folklore, Leprechauns were described wearing bright red coats, not green.
facts_and_myths.explanation: 18th- and 19th-century accounts described Leprechauns wearing red coats with pointed tricorn hats; green was popularized in modern times.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name comes from Old Irish 'luchorpan', meaning 'little body'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Leprechauns live in large noisy underground cities with thousands of families.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Leprechauns are strictly solitary creatures who live alone in hollow trees or under hedges mending single shoes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: European Union law protected the Carlingford Lough leprechauns under the EU Habitats Directive.

name: Selkie
visual_anchor: Beautiful dark-eyed maiden shedding a glistening mottled seal skin on a windswept Scottish coastal reef under a full moon.
core_traits: Mythological creatures found in Scottish, Irish, and Faroese coastal folklore
Live as seals in the ocean but shed their seal skin to become breathtaking human beings on land
If a mortal man steals and conceals a female Selkie's seal skin, she is forced to become his human wife
Always yearns deeply for the sea, immediately returning to the ocean the moment she discovers her hidden skin

facts_and_myths.claim: A Selkie wife who finds her stolen skin will abandon her mortal family and return to the ocean forever.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The traditional folk ballad recounts that even with loving human children, the call of the ocean is irresistible once her skin is found.
